notes.summary: Raw all-support envelopes, graded ideals and actual decreasing-D closure.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves raw positivity iff continuity, the actual J_k/factorial formula, decreasing-D closure by insertion before energy, and exact primary-gauge covariance. No increasing closure is assumed.
notes.text:
Use the ENTIRE qualified G331. For an excellent local reduction R and proper primary gauge a, X={v:v(a)=1} retains every semivaluation support. The independent geometric core consists of actual negative effective real Cartier presentations on actual primary blowups, with nonnegative degree on every contracted proper integral curve. C is its finite continuous uniform closure; D is its actual decreasing-C-net completion, including bottom. G331 grants the geometric/ideal comparison, topology, density, finite maxima, addition/scaling and full positive descent, but no envelope theorem.

For finite continuous phi, let p=sup{h in D:h<=phi}. Negative primary constants bound p below. If g_alpha decreases to an admissible h, the increasing open sets {g_alpha<phi+epsilon} cover compact X. One common index works globally, so g_alpha-epsilon is a C minorant at least h-epsilon. Therefore raw C and D suprema agree and p is finite lower semicontinuous. If p is continuous, the sets {g>p-epsilon}, over C minorants, have a finite subcover; their finite maximum approximates p uniformly, so p belongs to C. Conversely p in D is upper semicontinuous and hence continuous. For p*(x)=inf_{open U containing x}sup_U p, continuity of phi gives p<=p*<=min(phi,0). Thus p* belongs to D iff p*=p is continuous. A greatest D minorant exists exactly then. Downward shifts prove uniform nonexpansivity.

Define the actual ideal J_k(phi)={f:v(f)>=-k phi(v) for EVERY v in X}. It contains a^ceil(kM), where M>=max(0,-min phi). It is proper primary if phi is negative somewhere, and unit otherwise. It is integrally closed: a violated inequality in an ideal-integrality equation makes the leading power the unique finite least-valued term, impossible after passing first to the support quotient. Noetherianity gives finite generation of each ideal, not of its graded algebra. J_k J_l is contained in J_{k+l}, and J_k^l in J_{kl}. Hence -v(J_{n!})/(n!) increases. Its supremum is p: rationally approximate any C minorant, subtract a small rational primary constant after synchronizing denominators, and obtain a single-ideal minorant arbitrarily close below it. Its ideal lies in the corresponding J_k; sufficiently large factorials are divisible by k. This proves pointwise convergence only.

D is closed under decreasing D-nets by insertion. On a normal local domain set u=inf_i u_i. If u vanishes anywhere, the granted normal zero dichotomy makes every u_i zero. Otherwise a nonzero term is uniformly <=-c for finite c>0, by compact upper semicontinuity. Given finite continuous F>u, compact increasing covers {u_i<F} select a tail term below F everywhere. Its ONE actual C representation supplies g<F and g<-c/2 everywhere. Choose small b>0 with b||g||<min(F-g). Then q=(1-b)g belongs to C and u<q<F, including bottom points. Strict C majorants are downward directed by insertion into their continuous minimum. Their infimum is u: Urysohn cutoffs supply F>u with F(x)<t for every finite t>u(x), including at bottom, followed by insertion. Reverse pointwise order gives ONE actual decreasing C-net. Finite products treat semilocal normal centres; pulling to normalization and using G331 full-fibre D descent proves the assertion for every excellent reduced germ. This grants no increasing or nondirected-infimum closure. Only afterwards may qualified E350's existing-D energy criterion be applied.

For another primary b, d(v)=v(b)>0 and H(v)=v/d(v) are bounded continuous section data. Transport BOTH obstacles and potentials by phi_b(Hv)=phi_a(v)/d(v). The competitor order bijection gives p_b(phi_b)(Hv)=p_a(phi_a)(v)/d(v). J_k inequalities divide by the same factor, so the ideals are unchanged. Bounded upper regularization also transports by continuity of 1/d. This is the exact one-factor cocycle. Nilpotents are reduced away; dimension zero has the empty boundary; unit gives zero; nonprimary partial sections receive no compact global assertion. Lower-dimensional centres and all supports remain fibre data.

notes.text:
Use G331 and n1. Let R be an excellent normal local DOMAIN of dimension two, with arbitrary residue field k and characteristic. The product blowup of finitely chosen primary ideals, including a, dominates their blowups and is integral projective and the identity off the closed point. Normalize finitely. Excellence makes the nonregular locus closed; normality puts it in codimension at least two, hence it is finite on this surface. Its normal local completions are normal by current Stacks0C23 at normal formal fibres. These are exactly condition(4) of CURRENT54.14.5, tags0BGP/0BGJ. The complete implication(4)->(3) and normalized-blowup construction give a regular projective integral T principalizing the chosen ideals, still the identity on the punctured spectrum. No SNC or higher-dimensional resolution is asserted.

Current0AY8 applies: proper T over integral normal R, reduced dominating generic component, generic H0=Frac(R). Thus Gamma(T,O)=R and the closed fibre is geometrically connected. Regular local factoriality makes its exceptional integral curves E_i Cartier. Write E_a=sum b_i E_i, b_i=ord_Ei(a)>0, with a O_T=O_T(-E_a). This Cartier divisor supports the ENTIRE closed fibre; there are no isolated fibre points.

Set M_ij=deg_k(O_T(E_j)|E_i). Off-diagonal entries are local intersection lengths times actual residue degrees, so M is symmetric with nonnegative off-diagonal entries and connected graph. Pullback of the ample tautological bundle on Bl_a gives M b<=0, with some strict entry. Indeed Bl_a must have a fibre curve: otherwise proper quasi-finiteness would make it finite and an isomorphism over normal R, making a principal, contrary to the primary height bound in dimension two. A T-curve dominating a fibre curve gives strict degree positivity.

For A=-M and t_i=b_i z_i, direct expansion gives t^T A t=sum_i(Ab)_i b_i z_i^2+sum_{i<j}(-A_ij)b_i b_j(z_i-z_j)^2. Equality forces z constant along the connected graph and zero at a strict entry. Thus A is positive definite. Every principal A_J has nonpositive off-diagonal entries and nonnegative inverse: if A_J x=y>=0 and x=x_+-x_- with disjoint nonnegative parts, nonzero x_- would give x_-^T y=x_-^T A_J x_+-x_-^T A_J x_-<0. Moreover A^-1 1 is strictly positive; a zero coordinate would give a nonpositive row value. Its rational entries can be cleared to positive integers d_i with M d<0.

D0=sum d_i E_i is actual effective Cartier. O_T(-D0) has positive degree on every closed-fibre curve. COMPLETE current0B5Y applies to the FULL proper fibre, including nonreduced structure and imperfect residue field, and proves ampleness. COMPLETE current30.21.4/0D2N gives relative ampleness near the closed point, hence on the whole local base. Serre generation/coherence and a high very ample power give N for which L^N, L=O_T(-D0), is generated and defines a closed immersion.

I=Gamma(T,L^N) is a finite ideal inside Gamma(T,O)=R, unit off the closed point and proper because it vanishes on the boundary; hence primary. Generation gives I O_T=L^N. Choose ideal generators containing the immersion sections. Adding generators preserves the closed immersion by the graph of their additional ratios and properness. T and ACTUAL Bl_I are integral closed subschemes of the same projective space agreeing with the identical dense punctured graph. Their prime ideals are determined by that graph, so both are its scheme-theoretic closure and T=Bl_I. This applies to every regular common refinement built from finitely chosen primary models, without arbitrary-proper-model cofinality.

Complete immediate statements/proofs of0BGJ/0BGP,0C23,0AY8,0B5Y,current0D2N and0B5S were read. notes.summary: Full normal surface envelopes follow from actual nef projection and a greatest finite vector.
notes.detailedSummary: Dominates every core, C and bounded D competitor on all supports, clamps unbounded competitors, and proves a MAX-stable polytope has a greatest vector. Density yields every finite continuous obstacle.
notes.text:
Use G331 and n1-n2. Fix regular ACTUAL primary T with E_a=sum b_i E_i. A core competitor on another primary model pulls to a regular common ACTUAL primary refinement T'. Let D' be its negative effective real curve-nef Cartier divisor, mu:T'->T, and D=mu_*D'. On regular T this negative exceptional divisor is Cartier. Effective Cartier pullback mu*E_i is a nonnegative sum of contracted curves. Actual surface projection and Cartier symmetry give D.E_i=D'.mu*E_i>=0. Projection is checked on each curve: point image gives degree zero; curve image gives degree times function-field degree. This uses complete0AYA divisor-CYCLE projection before a global Chow quotient, retaining residue weights.

F=D'-mu*D is supported on mu-exceptional curves, since proper birational maps of normal surfaces are isomorphisms at generic codimension-one points. Its intersections there are nonnegative. The relevant principal negative matrix has nonpositive inverse by n2; hence every coefficient of F is <=0. Thus F is ACTUALLY negative effective and h_D'<=h_D on ALL supports. Evaluation first passes to Frac(R/support(v)) and lifts its valuation-ring morphism from the punctured generic point by properness. Effective exceptional equations then have finite nonnegative values. No fraction-field map to the support quotient is assumed. The projected coefficients are exactly c_i=b_i h_D'(nu_i), nu_i=ord_Ei/b_i.

For h in C, uniform core approximants give c_i=b_i h(nu_i), c_i<=0 and M c>=0. At every valued centre v(E_i)>=0 is finite and sum b_i v(E_i)=1. Thus projected evaluations converge uniformly, with error bounded by max_i|delta c_i|/b_i, and h<=sum c_i v(E_i). For bounded D use its ONE specified decreasing C-net; the finitely many coefficient limits are finite and commute with the finite evaluation sum. An unbounded competitor below f>=-B clamps to max(h,-B), whose actual representation max(g_alpha,-B) proves bounded D membership and remains below f.

For a finite signed primary-profile obstacle f, principalize its finite ideals and a on T. Actual evaluation gives f(v)=sum b_i f(nu_i)v(E_i). The compact polytope -B b_i<=c_i<=min(0,b_i f(nu_i)), M c>=0 contains -B b. It is coordinate-MAX stable: in row i choose the vector attaining the maximal ith coordinate; its diagonal term stays unchanged and every other coordinate increases with a nonnegative off-diagonal coefficient. Take a maximizer of each coordinate and their finite maximum. This is a greatest vector c*. The negative effective nef Cartier divisor sum c*_i E_i evaluates to H* in the geometric core and below f on every support. Every D competitor, after clamping and projection, has a feasible vector and is <=H*. Hence H* is the FULL envelope, not merely a model-restricted one.

Signed primary profiles are uniformly dense in all real continuous functions by G331. N1 nonexpansivity makes their positive envelopes uniformly Cauchy and convergent to the full raw envelope of any continuous phi. Closedness of C proves P(phi) in C. Thus EVERY excellent normal local surface, in all residue fields and characteristics including mixed characteristic, has continuous greatest geometric envelopes. The surface nef-pushforward argument is not transferred to higher dimension.

notes.summary: Continuous envelopes on isolated normal closed algebraic characteristic-zero germs in every dimension.
notes.detailedSummary: Uses the qualified three-author BdFF source, clears Cartier denominators, handles zero and unit corrections, and converts upper coefficient approximation to uniformity through the finite determining trace. Every D competitor uses one actual C net before density.
notes.text:
Use only G331 and n1 plus the ordinary published applications stated here. R is the local ring at a CLOSED point of a normal algebraic variety over an ALGEBRAICALLY CLOSED characteristic-ZERO field, and the point is an ISOLATED singularity. All dimensions are allowed. Regular germs are treated separately by exact BFJ in n5; normal curves are DVRs and dimension zero is empty. Finite primary generators and models spread to a neighbourhood with cosupport only at the point, so localization is legitimate.

The source is THREE-author Boucksom-de Fernex-Favre, The volume of an isolated singularity, Duke2012, not the four-author BdFFU paper. Complete immediate setting/sign,1.8/1.12,2.9-2.13 including ENTIRE2.12 proof,2.15-2.17,3.12-3.17 and4.1-4.11 were read. Supplied PDF pages22/41/46/47 were physically viewed to check directions. Recursive characteristic-zero resolution, singular/asymptotic multiplier ideals, compatible boundaries, Takagi subadditivity and numerical b-divisor foundations are disclosed published inputs, not freshly reconstructed historical proofs.

Use Z(I)_E=-ord_E(I). Every G331 core gives a source-nef Cartier b-divisor: normalize its actual primary determination and apply the point/positive-degree curve pullback rule. If core functions converge uniformly to h in C, their coefficients converge to H_E=ord_E(a)h(ord_E/ord_E(a)), and every base trace is zero. COMPLETE1.12(a) converts coefficient convergence with this fixed finite-dimensional base-trace space into numerical convergence on each fixed model. Closedness of the source nef cone makes H source-nef. No converse recognition of arbitrary source-nef divisors as D functions is assumed.

For a rational signed primary-profile obstacle f, use an ACTUAL normalized product blowup Y principalizing its finite ideals and a. Its rational exceptional Cartier b-divisor C is determined there. Let E_i be its finitely many exceptional primes, b_i=ord_Ei(a)>0. Actual order units give M Z(a)<=C. COMPLETE2.13/2.15/2.17 yield W=Env_X(C)=Env_pi(C_pi), with M Z(a)<=W<=C. Its base trace is zero, so source2.12 negativity gives W<=0. If W=0, f>=0 on divisors and hence everywhere by continuity and G331 density; its envelope is zero.

For W!=0 clear denominators BEFORE literal integral-Cartier4.11: apply it to N C with envelope N W, then rescale. It provides primary ideals b_k and rational q_k>0 with B_k=q_k Z(b_k)>=W and (B_k)_E->W_E coefficientwise. Their profiles u_k=-q_k v(b_k) are actual geometric core functions. Mandatory qualifications: Jacobian/defect corrections have cosupport contained in the point and are UNIT-or-primary; the defect may be unit in the Gorenstein case. Multiplier ideals may initially be unit but become proper eventually because some W coefficient is negative. Discard a finite prefix. If the positive correction c is real, round UP to an integer: W<=0 preserves Z(b_k)>=(k+c)W and gives rational scaling. The source inequalities are Z(b_k)>=kW+Z(defect)+Z(Jac), correction>=c_0 Z(m), and W<=epsilon Z(m). Isolation supplies the primary correction bound. These are only coefficientwise estimates.

Set eta_k=max_i((B_k)_Ei-C_Ei)^+/b_i and eps_k=eta_k+1/k. Since W_Ei<=C_Ei, eta_k->0. The source-nef B_k+eps_k Z(a) has trace <=C_pi, hence is <=W by largest-trace2.13. Thus on every centred divisor u_k-eps_k<=W_E/ord_E(a)<=u_k. Pairwise bounds |u_k-u_l|<=eps_k+eps_l extend from dense divisors to ALL supports because both profiles are continuous. They converge uniformly to U in C, whose divisor coefficients are W. W<=C and continuity give U<=f everywhere. Only now is a full-support function attached to W constructed.

For EVERY h=inf_alpha h_alpha in D below f, use its ONE actual C representation. For eps>0 one common index satisfies h_alpha(nu_i)<=f(nu_i)+eps at all finitely many vertices, including bottom limits. Its source-nef H_alpha+eps Z(a) has trace <=C_pi, hence <=W. Therefore h_alpha-eps<=U on divisors, then everywhere by continuity/density. Since h<=h_alpha, letting eps->0 gives h<=U. This avoids bounding USC spikes by density alone. U is the FULL greatest D minorant. Dense rational signed obstacles and n1 nonexpansivity give every finite continuous obstacle; n5 gives extended-USC and decreasing-net consequences.

This proves the stated isolated normal closed algebraic, algebraically closed characteristic-zero sector in ANY dimension. It does not cover general nonisolated, positive/mixed characteristic, nonclosed, other-residue-field or nonalgebraic excellent higher-dimensional germs. No higher-dimensional nef pushforward or arbitrary-model cofinality is asserted. Artifacts: n4.md, whole-source-application-ledger.md and retained p43-p48 source bodies/pixels. notes.detailedSummary: Uses substantive closed-face continuity, every retraction and the complete fixed-complex 3.18/3.22 estimate. After CE is established, one continuous-majorant net gives poles and full decreasing-obstacle-net stability.
notes.text:
Use G331 and n1; n3-n4 supply independently proved CE sectors. BFJ, Valuations and plurisubharmonic singularities, applies in Sections1-4 to a smooth AFFINE CLOSED germ over an ALGEBRAICALLY CLOSED characteristic-ZERO field, dimension>=2. For an obstacle h determined on one dual complex, clamp nef coefficient competitors above -M and take their finite maxima and bounded coefficientwise limit in the source closed max-stable nef cone. Its envelope W has function g continuous on every CLOSED simplex by3.11, whose proof uses multiplier profiles and bounded thinness on that simplex. Interior convexity alone is insufficient. The canonical extension g(v)=inf_pi g(r_pi v) and2.7 give all-support order. Coefficient order on the determining complex extends by closed-face continuity and rational divisorial density, then every retraction; hence -M<=g<=min(h,0), and G331's exact BFJ specialization puts every D competitor below g.

For W=0 use unit. Otherwise complete3.18(iii), with k=j+C, gives W_j<=W<=j/(j+C)W_j, W_j=Z(L^infinity(jW))/j. C is finite for this fixed envelope/complex, not globally bounded thinness. The full proof uses3.22 and smooth multiplier subadditivity. Section ideals contain completed boundary powers and are proper because a coefficient is negative. G331 contracts them exactly. Their profiles g_j extend the coefficient inequalities over all closed faces and ALL retractions, giving g_j<=g and g_j>=(1+C/j)g, hence 0<=g-g_j<=MC/j uniformly on the entire boundary. Thus g belongs to C. Signed rational ideal obstacles principalize on a common simple modification in the exact source domain; density and nonexpansivity give every continuous obstacle. This is equality with the published determining nef envelope and its continuous uniform extension. DVR/empty cases are direct, and gauges follow n1.

On ANY germ with CE, let phi be bounded-above extended USC and phi'=min(phi,0). Let F range over finite continuous phi'<=F<=0. This family contains zero, is downward directed by minimum, and has infimum phi'. At phi'(x)<t<=0 choose finite phi'(x)<c<t and a cutoff chi supported in {phi'<c}, equal to one at x. Then c chi>=phi' everywhere and has value c at x. Zero coordinates and bottom values are handled directly. The envelopes P(F) form ONE actual decreasing C-net. Its infimum H belongs to D by definition, is below phi and dominates every D minorant termwise. It is the greatest envelope, USC and possibly with poles. Bounded outputs are existing bounded D, so qualified E350 supplies energy and genuine open-exception quasicontinuity; general finite-energy membership requires its criterion on this already-D limit.

For a decreasing net phi_i of bounded-above USC obstacles with limit phi, monotonicity gives P(phi)<=inf_i P(phi_i). For continuous F>=phi', F<=0, and eps>0, the increasing OPEN sets {min(phi_i,0)<F+eps} cover compact X. One common index works everywhere, giving P(phi_i)<=P(F+eps)<=P(F)+eps by a legitimate negative shift of competitors. Take inf_i, eps->0 and inf_F to obtain equality. The limit is identified with the ONE-net construction, so no arbitrary-infimum closure is assumed. This proves full decreasing-USC-obstacle NET stability, including poles, on CE sectors. Gauge covariance, zero/bottom and idempotence follow from the competitor order bijection.

notes.text:
Use G331 and n1,n3-n5. Let A be excellent normal local domain and A inject into finite reduced B whose EVERY minimal component dominates A. Retain all marked semilocal centres and supports. Exceptional equations remain regular on dominating reduced components; effectivity and the point/positive-degree curve rule pull back. Support-quotient evaluation composes correctly. Uniform and actual decreasing limits preserve C,D pullback.

For a dominating domain component with fields K subset L, choose finite normal M/K containing all embedding images and normalize A in M to E. Excellence makes it finite. Let G=Aut_K(M), q=[M:K]/|G|, allowing inseparability. G331's norm factorization, generic inseparable length, quotient-support Gauss coefficient minima and density identify its kernel as q sum_{sigma in G}delta_{w composed with sigma} for ANY lift w. Choice independence and full-fibre support force this orbit to be the ENTIRE E/A fibre. Every B/A point lifts to E. Thus fibres are finite and G is transitive on full fibres, including nonminimal supports; no defectless ramification formula is assumed.

For H in C_B, restrict to a domain component, pull to E and take the finite maximum of G-translates. It is C_E and full-fibre constant, so positive descent gives a C_A function equal to the maximum over that component fibre. Finite maximum over dominating components gives MH(v)=max_{rho(w)=v}H(w) in C_A. Every source semivaluation lies on a minimal component. For an actual H_alpha decreasing to H in D, finite fibres and directedness give max_w inf_alpha H_alpha(w)=inf_alpha max_w H_alpha(w), including bottom; one common index meets every finite strict threshold. Hence MH belongs to D through ONE C representation. No vertical component receives a fabricated degree.

For K=C or D, H<=f rho implies MH<=f and H<=rho*(MH); base competitors pull back conversely. Thus unrestricted RAW envelopes satisfy P_B^K(f rho)=rho*P_A^K(f), even before positivity. If source centres have CE, the source continuous envelope is fibre constant and positive descent proves CE on A. Alternatively its normalized positive full-fibre average p lies in C_A, dominates all target competitors, and rho*p<=U. Since p is a positive average no greater than any fibre value U(w), all finite values equal p. This argument does not average extended bottoms to force constancy. USC commutation follows by pulling back n5's ONE continuous-majorant net and testing every source competitor termwise.

A nonflat example over any field is A=k[U,V,W]_(m)/(UW-V^2) inside B=k[x,y]_(x,y), U=x^2,V=xy,W=y^2. Normality follows from k[x^2,xy,y^2]=k[M] intersect k[x,y], M={(i,j):i+j even}, in k(x,y), an intersection of normal rings. The finite dominating extension has degree two, but closed fibre basis 1,x,y and dimension three, since m_A B=(x,y)^2; it is not flat rank two. Surface CE covers it in every characteristic. Adjoining smooth variables over algebraically closed characteristic zero gives normal NONISOLATED higher-dimensional targets with an actual smooth cover and CE. No universal good-cover theorem is claimed.

notes.summary: Explicit full-normalization formula and exact finite-continuous positive domain.
notes.detailedSummary: Primary conductor masks and compact quotient topology give fibre MAX under normal-centre CE. Positivity is equivalent to full-fibre constancy/continuous raw envelope. No unconditional extended-USC or pole formula is claimed.
notes.text:
Use G331 and n1,n3-n6. Let S normalize an excellent reduced local R, separated into ALL marked normal centres, rho:X_S->X_R its compact quotient, c its conductor. Finite conductor value gives singleton fibres; infinite value gives exactly restriction over R/c subset S/c, including internal, nonpure and nonminimal supports. Positive C,D descent is full-fibre constancy.

For finite continuous phi, downstairs raw pullback is the supremum of full-fibre-constant source minorants. Choose B>0 with -B<=phi and clamp a source C minorant g into [-B,0]. The actual unit-or-primary K_N=c+a^N supplies b_N(v)=-(B/N)min(v(c),N). It is between -B and zero and equals -B both at infinity AND at finite v(c)>=N. Then max(g+b_N rho,-B) remains below phi rho and is full-fibre constant, since every nontrivial fibre has infinite conductor and value -B. It positively descends. At finite conductor value the mask tends to zero, proving p_R rho=p_S there. This locus is dense upstairs: the conductor contains a regular element, finite at fraction-field divisors, and G331 proves all-support divisorial density.

Assume EVERY normal centre has CE. N3 proves this in dimension two; a DVR has a one-point boundary with actual closed-point Cartier clipping, and dimension zero is empty. Thus all excellent reduced germs of dimension<=2 qualify. N4-n6 give further isolated/smooth/actual-cover sectors. U=P_S(phi rho) is continuous, p_R rho<=U everywhere and equal on the dense finite-conductor locus. Hence (p_R rho)*=U on ALL supports by continuity.

For any bounded-above F on a compact quotient, F*(v)=max_{rho(w)=v}(F rho)*(w). One inequality follows from continuity of rho. For the reverse, a threshold t above the compact-fibre maximum admits finitely many neighbourhoods covering the fibre where pullback suprema are <t. The complement is compact and has closed image missing v; its complementary base neighbourhood has entire inverse image in that union. Hence its F supremum is <t. Let t decrease. No openness of rho is needed. Therefore E_R(phi):=p_R*(v)=max_{rho(w)=v}U(w), even outside positivity.

Equivalent conditions are: E_R in D_R; p_R continuous in C_R and equal to E_R; U constant on EVERY full fibre; the displayed fibre maximum continuous. N1 gives the first equivalence. Continuous pullbacks agreeing with U densely agree everywhere. Positive C descent supplies the converse. Continuity of the fibre maximum similarly forces its pullback to equal U densely and everywhere. Outside this domain no maximal D minorant exists: finite max with every competitor would force a maximal member to equal the non-USC raw supremum.

Without normal-centre CE, the exact finite-continuous criterion remains p_R* in D_R iff unrestricted raw p_S is continuous AND full-fibre constant. Necessity follows because continuous p_R rho<=p_S agrees densely, while lower semicontinuity of p_S along an approaching net gives the reverse inequality everywhere. Sufficiency is positive descent. Unknown normal continuity therefore remains a condition outside proved sectors.

E_R is uniformly nonexpansive, including outside its positive domain, by source nonexpansivity and fixed-fibre maxima. The positive domain is uniformly closed because constancy passes through uniform limits. Gauge transport divides every lift by the SAME positive base factor, so fibre MAX obeys precisely the one-factor cocycle. No conductor fibre is replaced by a generic or capacity-a.e. test.

For EXTENDED bounded-above USC obstacles the source envelope may only be D and discontinuous or have poles. Dense equality does not then supply the continuity step; NO unconditional fibre-maximum formula follows. Always valid is the constrained raw-D identity: base pullback equals the supremum of full-fibre-constant source D minorants. A fibre-constant source greatest minorant descends; when both greatest envelopes exist, commutation is equivalent to source fibre constancy. Base existence alone is not promoted to an unrestricted pole formula.

notes.detailedSummary: The double-plane raw envelope is explicitly non-USC despite continuous normal-centre envelopes. Its regularization remains below the obstacle but is not positive. This does not settle the normal higher-dimensional residual.
notes.text:
Use G331 and n1,n7. Over ANY field let R=k[x,y,z]_(m)/(xy), normalization A times B with A=k[x,z]_(x,z), B=k[y,z]_(y,z), maximal-ideal gauge. The ring is their fibre product over k[z]_(z): polynomial pairs with common residue are f+g-h, and local unit denominators clear by their residue units. The conductor is (x)A times(y)B. Its sole identified boundary pair is q_A killing x and q_B killing y, both with z-order one; downstairs support (x,y) is nonminimal.

The finite continuous obstacle phi=-1-1/v(y), reciprocal infinity zero, restricts to -1 on A and -1-1/w(y) on B, in [-2,-1], and agrees at that pair. On B, every normalized centred w satisfies w(f)>=ord_mB(f). Thus every D_B function g obeys g(w)<=g(o_B), first for ideal profiles, then uniform and actual decreasing limits. Since phi(o_B)=-2, its B envelope is constant -2; A envelope is -1. The continuous source tuple (-1,-2) is incompatible.

For n>=1 use A-primary J_n=(x^n,xz^(n-1),z^(2n)), paired with -2 on B. Its profiles agree at the identified pair and positively descend. Writing a=w(x),b=w(z),min(a,b)=1, the A profile is -1 if a<=b, -min(1+(a-1)/n,2) if a>b finite, and -2 at q_A. At n=1 the middle generator is literally x. These increase and show the exact base raw envelope is -1 on A except q_A, and -2 at the common point and throughout B. The obstacle and universal B order bound give matching upper bounds for EVERY D competitor.

Monomial weights x=L,z=1 converge on localized polynomials to q_A, so the raw envelope is not USC. It has no greatest or maximal D minorant. Its regularization has common-point value -1 but B-order-point value -2, violating the same D_B inequality, and is not positive although below phi. N7 reproduces it by full-fibre MAX. This is an exact nonnormal obstruction, not a normal counterexample.

More generally a fibre joining distinct positive-dimensional normal centres prevents universal CE. Select a finite-conductor divisorial point on one centre, whose singleton base image is disjoint from the compact images of other centres. A continuous obstacle in [-1,0] can be -1 there and zero on those other images. On the first centre the granted inequality g(nu)>=K g(w) forces competitors at the selected fibre point <=-1/K; on the second the envelope is zero. Source envelopes cannot be fibre constant, so n7 excludes positive base regularization. Internal fibres are not classified by this argument.

notes.text:
Use qualified G331/B341/E350 and n1. B341 supplies bounded ideal moments; E350 supplies their independently geometric identification, F(u,v)=integral(-u)dmu(v)>=0, E=-F/n, capacity and Cauchy at existing-D/E1 hypotheses. The mandatory SH17.4.7 quotient-annihilator and ambient top-degree qualifications remain. No new source theorem is invoked.

On R=k[x,y]_(x,y), ANY field, J_0=R,J_j=(x,y^j) is ACTUAL graded, J_rJ_s subset J_{r+s}, with m^j subset J_j. The profiles u_j=-min(v(x)/j,v(y)) increase to -1 at the unique support-(x) point q and zero elsewhere. Monomial weights(L,1) approach q, so the exact limit is not USC/D; its regularization zero is already the good envelope of obstacle zero.

For ALL r,s>=0, product generators have exponents (r+s-i-h,ji+h),0<=i<=s,0<=h<=r. At column 0<=x<r+s the least y is r+s-x+(j-1)max(0,s-x). Summation proves length(R/m^rJ_j^s)=r(r+1)/2+rs+j s(s+1)/2. Hence e(m,J_j)=1,e(J_j)=j. Qualified identities give measure mass1/j, F(u_j,u_j)=1/j, E(u_j)=-1/(2j) increasing to zero. B=F, NOT -F; the historical positive-energy sign is rejected. For capacity tests phi in [-1,0] intersect D, Cauchy and F(phi,phi)<=1 give F(u_j,phi)<=1/sqrt(j), hence Cap{u_j<-eps}<=1/(eps sqrt(j)). Products converge in total variation to zero by their masses. These facts do not establish D membership of the increasing pointwise limit.

Next R=k[X,Y,Z]_(m)/(XY-Z^2)=k[s^2,st,t^2]_(m), ANY characteristic. It is normal because k[s^2,st,t^2]=k[M] intersect k[s,t], M={(i,j):i+j even}, an intersection of normal rings in its fraction field. Dimension two and cotangent dimension three show singularity. For a=v(X),b=v(Y), min(a,b)=1 and v(Z)=(a+b)/2, allowing infinity. The unique a=infinity point q kills(X,Z).

I_n=(X^n,XY^(n-1),Y^(2n)) gives u_n=-1 if a<=b, -min(1+(a-1)/n,2) if a>b finite, and -2 at q; at n=1 the middle generator is literally X. These increase in [-2,-1] to -1 off q and -2 at q. Semigroup weights X=L,Y=1,Z=(L+1)/2 approach q, so this limit is not USC/D; its regularization -1 is the good envelope of obstacle -1.

The m-blowup is regular with X,Y charts coordinates X,Z/X and Y,Z/Y covering the conic even in characteristic two. Its generic order o has X,Y,Z value one. O_conic(1) has degree two, so qualified E350 gives mu(-1)=2 delta_o. The function z=-v(X) belongs to D through -min(v(X),k) and has reference moment two. Thus Cap{a>T}<=2/T and Cap{q}=0. For 0<eps<1 the exact error set is {a>1+n eps}, of capacity <=2/(1+n eps); for eps>=1 it is empty. Even the non-D limit is quasicontinuous after removing the genuine OPEN set {a>T}. Exact support membership cannot be replaced by capacity equality.

Universal multiplicity: nonnegative even-parity monomials of total degree<2k number k^2, so e(m)=2. I_n generators have exponents A=(2n,0),B=(2,2n-2),C=(0,4n). The complement of their upward convex hull has polygon0,A,B,C and area2n^2+2n. Ideal-power exponents lie in the dilated hull. Conversely rounding down three convex-combination coefficients leaves at most two missing generators; a fixed shift(D,D), exceeding three times the largest coordinate, supplies them with a nonnegative even-parity remainder. Pure powers bound the quotient rectangle. Discrepancies lie in constant-width edge strips with O(k) lattice points; parity density is one-half with O(k) boundary error. Therefore length(R/I_n^k)=(n^2+n)k^2+O(k), e(I_n)=2n^2+2n. Thus F(u_n,u_n)=2+2/n and E(u_n)=-1-1/n increases to E(-1)=-1.

Both examples diagnose invalid increasing-membership and energy/capacity-to-membership inferences. Neither disproves normal envelopes.
